failures.criterion: Architect's ruling under the 'fix it here' rule (2026-10-26 13:54Z, envoy bacc93d9ac734fa44f1f32d36b043e7c): no way of ending a kvwatch subscription can panic the listener. The paths include a connection close or drain, nats.go's own unsubscribe, and End at shutdown, not only the watcher replacement round 2 deferred. The architect gave the implementer the design: kvwatch watches through the nats.go jetstream package's KV watcher, which has no init timer, with its own idle timer for the timed-out-scan re-read; writes stay on the legacy API.
failures.evidence: nats.go v1.50.0 kv.go:1138-1170: the legacy watcher's init timer callback sends on errCh under w.mu. pDone closes errCh under the same mutex and only Stops the timer, which does not wait for a callback already running. The message handler holds w.mu while it blocks on the full 256-entry updates channel, so a callback that fires then and loses the mutex to pDone sends on a closed channel. Red test, commit b8fcdb264eee: packages/envoy/internal/kvwatch/subscription_end_test.go TestASubscriptionEndingMidScanNeverPanics. It holds the cache's first record, closes the watcher's connection, and releases the record at moments swept across a 20 ms JetStream wait. `cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/kvwatch/ -run TestASubscriptionEndingMidScanNeverPanics -count=1` crashed the test binary in 7 of 7 runs at 57e48f1, in 0.8-3.2 s: 'panic: send on closed channel ... github.com/nats-io/nats.go.(*kvs).WatchFiltered.func2() .../nats.go@v1.50.0/kv.go:1151, created by time.goFunc'.
